title.narrative: Community-based conservation of Western hoolock gibbons in Pauk Sa Mountain, Myanmar

description.narrative: The purpose of this project is to contribute to the conservation of the globally endangered western hoolock gibbon through interventions to assist local communities in one priority site to address immediate threats to the species. This will be done by: 1) forming at least five village conservation groups in the lower slopes of the Pauk Sa range; 2) facilitating village conservation agreements for a core conservation zone with the 5 villages including resource use mapping to establish the extent of swidden agriculture, mapping key landscape features used by villagers to identify their fields, digitizing these maps and including land cover data to identify a core conservation area (will utilize a participatory workshop to accomplish this); 3) facilitating development of village land use plans (needed to provide a mechanism to control village land use, and to better cooperate with the Forest Department and other government departments on village development and sustainable forestry); 4) facilitating VCGs in the development of community forestry licenses (needed to allow for a mixture of production, protection and regeneration on state forest lands such as Reserve Forests and is intended as a mechanism to divest responsibilities and benefits of sustainable forest management to local communities); 5) distributing small village development grants for sustainable community forestry, agroforestry, and sustainable agriculture; 6) carrying out a conservation awareness effort (through village consultation efforts) to increase understanding of the values and threats to Myanmars natural history, and to justify the interventions proposed under the project; 7) mapping the habitat of the gibbons; 8) using standard population sampling techniques to estimate/confirm the populations of all groups in conjunction with habitat mapping under item 7; 8) habituating one gibbon group for ecological studies; and 9) studying tree phenology and carrying out baseline ecological surveys.
